verified: Checked 2026-09-25 against the documents themselves. partI, immediateNote, antecedentNote, partII, interval, mannerQuestion, injuryQuestion, manner, maternalQuestion, maternal, deliveryQuestion and deliveryOptions are the printed wording of ORGI Form No. 4 (the form prints 'as a consequences of'; the Physicians' Manual section 2.3.3 and WHO use 'as a consequence of', used here). Form No. 4 has three Part I lines, (a) to (c); the Manual (2.3.3) allows extra lines when the sequence has more than three stages. Form No. 4A has the same Part I, Part II and pregnancy questions but no manner of death question. modesOfDying: 'heart failure' and 'asthenia' from Form No. 4 and the Manual (1.3); 'respiratory failure' from the Manual (2.3.3) and Form 4 directions; 'cardiac arrest' from WHO 2015; the rest from the ICMR-NCDIR 2022 audit framework list of mechanisms of death that must not be written in Part I (cardio respiratory arrest, cardio respiratory failure, renal or kidney failure, shock, respiratory failure or arrest, heart failure, syncope, multi organ or system failure, asthenia or exhaustion, coma or brain failure); spacing variants of the same terms are included for matching. The ICMR list also pairs 'heart attack' with cardiac arrest; it is left out because myocardial infarction is a valid cause when stated specifically. vagueTerms: 'old age' and 'senility' from Form 4 directions and the Manual (2.6.3 item 19: not to be given if a more specific cause is known, Part II only if contributory); convulsions, diarrhoea, ascites, jaundice and debility from the Form 4 'symptomatic statement' direction; 'fever', also listed there, is in vagueAtStart instead, which the helper flags only when the lowest line starts with it, so that specific diseases such as dengue fever, enteric fever and rheumatic fever are not flagged; 'natural death', 'unconscious' and 'cva' from the ICMR-NCDIR 2022 framework. Added 2026-09-25: modesOfDying 'cardiopulmonary arrest' and 'cardio pulmonary arrest' (the same mechanism as cardio respiratory arrest), and 'multiple organ failure', 'multi organ dysfunction', 'multiorgan dysfunction', 'multiple organ dysfunction' and 'mods' (variants of multi organ or system failure in the ICMR-NCDIR list); vagueTerms 'pyrexia', 'fever of unknown origin', 'fever of unknown cause', 'pyrexia of unknown origin', 'puo', 'fuo', 'febrile illness', 'abdominal pain', 'pain abdomen', 'chest pain', 'altered sensorium' and 'altered mental status' as symptomatic statements under the same Form 4 direction (symptoms and ill-defined conditions, ICD-10 chapter XVIII); these are not listed word for word in the sources. The symptom tip is from the same Form 4 direction, and the Form 4A tip from the ORGI form titles and the difference noted above. maternalAge (15 to 49 years) from the Manual 2.5. medicoLegalNote from the Manual 1.4 and 2.4. tips from Form 4 directions, the Manual 2.3.2 to 2.3.5 and WHO 2015. The Manual text was read from the Tamil Nadu CRS copy at www.crstn.org because the censusindia.gov.in copy failed TLS verification.
partI: (b) Due to (or as a consequence of)
(c) Due to (or as a consequence of)
immediateNote: State the disease, injury or complication which caused death, not the mode of dying such as heart failure, asthenia, etc.
antecedentNote: Morbid conditions, if any, giving rise to the above cause, stating underlying conditions last
partII: Other significant conditions contributing to the death but not related to the disease or condition causing it
interval: Interval between onset and death approx.
maternalQuestion: If deceased was a female, was pregnancy the death associated with?
deliveryQuestion: If yes, was there a delivery?
medicoLegalNote: In violent deaths and other medico-legal cases the certificate may be completed by the medical examiner at the post-mortem stage; the hospital informs the Registrar of the fact of death.
tips: One condition per line, with disease names written in full and no abbreviations.
Line (a) is the disease, injury or complication that directly caused death, never a mode of dying such as heart failure, respiratory failure or cardiac arrest.
Never give a symptom such as fever, abdominal pain or altered sensorium as the underlying cause: name the disease, e.g. Plasmodium falciparum malaria or pulmonary tuberculosis rather than fever.
Each line is due to the condition on the line below it; the underlying cause, which started the sequence, goes on the lowest used line of Part I.
Give the approximate interval between onset and death for every condition, e.g. from birth, several years or unknown.
Part II holds other conditions that contributed but were not part of the sequence. Old age or senility goes only in Part II, and never when a more specific cause is known.
For injury or poisoning, state the nature of the injury and the external cause; if accident, suicide or homicide is not yet known, still fill in the cause and mark the manner Pending investigation.
Form No. 4 is for hospital in-patient deaths and Form No. 4A for deaths outside hospital (non-institutional); Form 4A has the same Part I and Part II but no manner of death question.
